yuinsk.text: YuiNSK is all sharp edges: matchup rating near the top, bravery and resistance both sitting near the top, and a cadence that never drops. The accuracy sits near the top, with headshots close behind, and the lifetime numbers match the matchups stride for stride. A player who turns up sharp in every fight, whatever the opposition.

yuinsv.text: YuiNSV plays a swift, high-volume game: first-rate on every line, and a blistering output. Bravery runs near the top, so the output holds up against stronger enemies. Sharp aim, and headshots account for a strong slice of the attempts. The consistency mark sits below average, the lone blemish on an otherwise strong record.

yuokilerdestroyer.text: YuOkIlErDestroyer plays at full sprint: sitting top shelf, with pace at the ceiling and fearless all the way through. The output holds firm as the opposition gets stronger, while the headshots land near the very top. A complete game, played without a single wasted motion.

yuokilerdestroyeremerald.text: YuOkIlErDestroyerEMERALD never backs down: bravery sits at the very peak, the adjusted rating rides high, the tempo never drops, and the staying power keeps up. The output is furious, the aim is deadly, and a healthy share of the shots land as headshots. The lifetime numbers agree, placing the career in the top ranks, and consistency holds in the middle.

younglingslayertr.text: YounglingSlayerTR fights at full tilt: a furious kill pace, activity to match, and a matchup rating near the top. The bravery rises as the enemies get tougher, the aim stays precise, and the headshot share lands near the top. Consistency dips low against the strongest third, and the opponent sample here is older and thinner — so read this one as a rough sketch, not the finished picture.

younglingslayersprotocoldroid.text: YounglingSlayersProtocolDroid plays at a blistering clip: the kill pace sits among the very best tracked, backed by top-rank activity, bravery, and resistance. Precise aim, frequent headshots, and the lifetime record backs the matchup picture. Against the strongest third, the edge softens to mid-pack — the one wrinkle in a first-rate card.

youyun.text: Youyun wins the long game: a matchup rating near the very top, a matchup kill-death ratio among the best tracked, and resistance that scarcely yields against the strongest opposition. Pace sits well above average while the aim stays middling, yet the results stay elite, which says the timing and judgment carry the day. A player who makes every fight count.

y9k.text: y9k runs a complete, high-pressure game: the rating leads a full house, with tempo, bravery, and resistance all landing in the upper tier, and the direct-fight kill-death line sitting there too. The headshot share is top-shelf while raw accuracy stays middle of the pack, so the damage comes from placement rather than volume. The lifetime board rates them a notch below the matchups, which still leaves a fearsome profile.

yuokilertr.text: YuOkIlErTR brings relentless pressure: tempo and bravery set the pace in the upper tier, resistance close behind; the matchup kill-death mark keeps up too. Consistency stays above average, so the game holds its nerve against the strongest third, and the headshot share sits top-shelf. The lifetime numbers agree, landing in the upper tier alongside the matchups.

yoooooootr.text: YOOOOOOOTR plays a swift, fearless game: rating, activity, bravery, resistance all near the very top, with pace and output among the highest tracked. The consistency mark sinks near the bottom, the one soft spot on an otherwise strong card. Take this as a sketch of a strong start: the opponent sample behind it is older and smaller.

yooooooovs.text: YOOOOOOOVS is a young account already playing at the very top: rating, activity, bravery, resistance all push near the summit. Pace and output sit among the highest tracked, with the lifetime board ranking them near the top too. Early read, but the consistency mark dips below average, the one wrinkle so far.

younglingslayer.text: YounglingSlayer brings thunder: top-shelf pace, a game that climbs with the opposition, and headshots landing near the very top. The aim is middling, yet the record stays strong, and the lifetime board matches the matchups. Take this as a rough sketch rather than a finished portrait — the opponent sample behind it is older and smaller.

yolothenyouquit.text: yolothenyouquit has been fighting since 2014, and the years show in the steadiness: top-tier in the matchups, measured in tempo, and bravery that endures as the opposition hardens. The skirmish kill-death score runs near the top. The edge stays firm against the sternest third. The lifetime board is far humbler, with the IvI line near the bottom — a veteran who still shows up ready for every fight.

yoooooooeu.text: YOOOOOOOEU arrived days ago and already fights like a fixture: top-tier in the matchups, scorching in tempo, and bravery holding as the field gets tougher. The one-on-one kill-death tally sits near the top, and the edge holds even against the sternest third. Career numbers read top-tier too, which is rare this early. Early read, but the start is impossible to ignore.

yyyyyoooo.text: YYYYYOOOO plays a front-foot game: top-tier in the matchups, unflagging in tempo, and bravery that keeps pace when the field hardens. The direct-fight kill-death record rides near the top. Career numbers sit above the pack, and the pace stays high whatever the opposition, which keeps the pressure on. A player who never lets the pressure drop.

ylbshenhuanc.text: YLBshenhuaNC wins fights the quiet way: upper tier in the matchup standings, accuracy near the very top, with resistance that refuses to bend. Headshots land at a middling rate, and the lifetime board sits just under the matchups. The strongest third leaves the results steady — a regular who makes the hard game look easy.

yoooooooooooooooom.text: yoooooooooooooooom brings a full-throttle game to every fight: a top-tier matchup rating, activity near the top, and bravery that grows with the opposition. The tempo stays high, the duel kill-death line sits above average, and the lifetime board trails the matchups a touch. A veteran who still sets the pace instead of chasing it.

ylbshenhuavs.text: Since 2017, YLBshenhuaVS has built a game with no holes in it: a matchup rating inside the top ten percent, resistance that barely gives ground against stronger opposition, while the edge barely thins against the toughest third. Headshots are the one ordinary line on the card; everything else sits well above average, and the veteran still makes every exchange expensive.

yoannblanger.text: Since 2013, yoannblanger has been the slow-burn surprise: a matchup rating sitting with the top ranks, resistance that weathers stronger opposition, and a direct-fight kill-death record near the top. The tempo lands mid-pack and the toughest third shaves a little off the edge, but the lifetime board holds well above average, and this veteran picks the moment and makes it count.

yuokiler.text: YuOkIlEr has fought since 2018 and still sets the pace: upper-tier matchup rating, a pace up near the top, and bravery that rises as the opposition hardens. Headshots land at a top-shelf rate, and the lifetime board tells the same story. The edge keeps its shape even against the hardest third. A veteran who still plays like the fight depends on them.

ylbgreen.text: YLBGreen has been at this since 2016, and the card shows a veteran still sharp: a matchup grade sitting with the leaders, resistance that barely moves, and a head-on kill-death line near the top too. The tempo stays above average, the edge holds above average against stronger opposition, and the headshots land above average. A veteran still playing at full tilt, with the lifetime board to match.

yywdga.text: yywdga is the definition of a reliable regular: well above average on every count of the matchup board, with the edge holding against the hardest third too. The headshots land above average while the accuracy sits mid-pack, and the lifetime numbers confirm the matchups. No fireworks, no weak links — just a fighter who shows up, holds ground, and makes every fight a grind for the other side.

yersin.text: Yersin plays the complete game without a headline: well above average across the matchups, unbothered as the opposition hardens, and sharp where it counts. The aim runs ordinary, but the headshots land more often than most. A veteran regular who makes every fight a little harder than expected.

yourhelmetfailedinspection.text: YourHelmetFailedInspection is a young account with a loud, confident card: the matchup rating runs well above average, tempo and bravery keep pace, and resistance matches them, with accuracy to match. The one crack in the glass is consistency, which sinks toward the bottom when the opposition gets hardest — the edge thins when the opposition gets hardest. Early days, but the opening chapters already read like a regular on the rise.

yicitty.text: YiCitty plays a fast, front-foot game: activity and bravery riding near the top, accuracy and headshots near the top too, and a kill pace that never lets up. The lifetime board sits near the top as well, backing the matchups. The one wrinkle: the edge settles mid-pack when the opposition gets toughest, so the brightest moments come against softer opposition.

yogsothothtr.text: Since 2012, YogSothothTR has been a model of staying power: matchup rating, pace, bravery, resistance, aim, headshots — all of it well above average, year after year. The kill-death column of the matchups agrees, and the lifetime numbers tell the same story. More than a decade in, the card still reads like a regular at the top of their game.

yeting.text: Yeting brings a sharp, confident game: well above average in the matchups, precise with the shots, and unfazed when the opposition gets stronger. The lifetime board is cooler on them than the matchups are, which keeps the story honest. Against the very toughest third, though, some of the shine comes off — the one soft seam in an otherwise strong card.

yhzx006.text: Yhzx006 shoots straight and pays for it nowhere except the toughest fights: the aim sits near the top, the matchup rating well above average, and the results hold up against ordinary opposition. Against the strongest third the edge falls away sharply, headshots almost never land, and the lifetime IvI drops to near the bottom. A fighter with a sharp eye and one hard lesson still to learn.

yjsxiaofengcn.text: YJSxiaofengCN has been around since 2013, and the card is quietly strong: rating, tempo, and nerve all run above the middle. The resistance meets harder-hitting enemies head-on. They close out direct fights ahead more often than not, the headshots land below the middle, and the lifetime board sits below it too. A veteran regular whose matchup game keeps outrunning the career numbers.

youvebeenhitbyasmoothcriminal.text: YouveBeenHitByaSmoothCriminal is a fresh name with a loud opening: the tempo runs at the very top, the aim is among the sharpest tracked, and headshots land near the top too. The matchup rating sits above the middle, the nerve holds firm as enemies get tougher, the duel balance sheet runs strongly their way, and the lifetime board sits right at the top. Early read, but the first pages are hard to ignore — though versus the toughest third the edge gives ground.

yoshimitsutr.text: YoshimitsuTR is the definition of a solid regular: well above the middle in the matchups, a steady tempo, and calm as the opposition hardens. The faceoff books balance out mid-table, the lifetime numbers run above average, and the headshot share holds above the middle. No fireworks, just a card that holds together in every corner.

yjspibo314.text: YJSpibo314 plays a solid, unspectacular game that keeps paying off. The adjusted marks sit well above average, the pace runs brisk, and the edge holds steady under sterner pressure. The head-to-head returns rest just short of mid-pack, and the lifetime board lines up with the matchups. A dependable regular who turns up, digs in, and rarely gives anything away.

yumils.text: yuMILs wins the fights in front of them and cedes the ones at the top: a clear step above the middle overall, hard to budge in a straight fight, and up on the matchup count more often than not. The career kill tally sits well above the middle, matching the recent form. Only against the very strongest opposition does the edge slip — the single soft spot in a solid game. A strong regular who keeps the fight honest without ever needing the spotlight.

yorha2btt.text: Yorha2bTT plays the long, patient game: well above average on the matchup side, steady when the pressure builds, and calm against the hardest third too. The lifetime figures come in a touch below the matchup return, and headshots stay thin on the ground, so the strength is in staying power rather than flash. A dependable regular who makes every duel cost something.
